exam.title: Red Hat Certified Specialist in Cloud-native Development
exam.study_prerequisites: Red Hat recommends DO378 or equivalent Quarkus experience, strong Java SE skills including exceptions/annotations/collections, VS Code or VSCodium familiarity on RHEL, and beneficial OpenShift/Kafka familiarity. Build one complete service with the Red Hat Quarkus 3.8 BOM and practice configuration, resilience, health, metrics, JWT, REST, Panache, messaging, OpenAPI, REST clients and OpenTelemetry through package-mode restart.

review.notes: All 11 unweighted EX378 coding groups were reconciled with Red Hat Build of Quarkus 3.8 documentation and the archived upstream 3.8 guide set. The guide evolves one persistent service so configuration, resilience, health, metrics, MP-JWT, RESTEasy Reactive/Jakarta REST, Panache/JPA, Reactive Messaging, OpenAPI, REST Client Reactive and OpenTelemetry are tested together. Three scenarios, eight safe labs and 40 original checks include negative/failure paths, database and acknowledgment evidence, non-blocking boundaries, telemetry correlation and package-mode restart. All nine URLs are cataloged: seven reachable and O'Reilly plus Udemy automation-blocked; none missing or broken. Newer resources have an explicit 3.8 API/name gap checklist and no recalled exam tasks are used.

findings.title: Objective monitor omitted most Quarkus tasks
findings.evidence: A substring Readiness end marker matched a health objective, truncating the accepted list before the remaining health and all later groups.
findings.recommendation: Use exact complete-heading matching, add a regression test, compare the full 64-task list to EX378V38K and explicitly replace the reviewed baseline. Lifecycle did not change.
findings.resolution: Use exact complete-heading matching, add a regression test, compare the full 64-task list to EX378V38K and explicitly replace the reviewed baseline. Lifecycle did not change.

findings.title: Configuration precedence needed concrete evidence
findings.evidence: Default source ordinals and profile resolution are distinct parts of effective configuration.
findings.recommendation: Add ordinal table, system/environment collision example, profile behavior and high-ordinal custom-source caveat.
findings.resolution: Add ordinal table, system/environment collision example, profile behavior and high-ordinal custom-source caveat.

findings.title: Health qualifiers and endpoints were too abstract
findings.evidence: Health Startup and runtime Startup serve different purposes; readiness, liveness, groups and wellness have different consumers.
findings.recommendation: Add qualified import distinction and default paths with management/root-path caveats.
findings.resolution: Add qualified import distinction and default paths with management/root-path caveats.

findings.title: Reactive signatures do not make blocking persistence safe
findings.evidence: Dispatch depends on return type, transaction and explicit blocking annotations.
findings.recommendation: Teach the worker/I/O boundary and add a synchronous transactional resource example.
findings.resolution: Teach the worker/I/O boundary and add a synchronous transactional resource example.

findings.title: Flush and durable completion needed separation
findings.evidence: Managed fields use dirty checking, while SQL flush can precede a later rollback.
findings.recommendation: Add real HTTP CRUD and explicit failed-after-flush rollback tests with committed row observations.
findings.resolution: Add real HTTP CRUD and explicit failed-after-flush rollback tests with committed row observations.

findings.title: Acknowledgment was conflated with committed connector progress
findings.evidence: Kafka throttled commits advance contiguous acknowledged positions periodically; database effects and Kafka progress are not automatically atomic.
findings.recommendation: Add crash/replay, out-of-order, auto-commit and failure-strategy cases; require transactional deduplication for external effects.
findings.resolution: Add crash/replay, out-of-order, auto-commit and failure-strategy cases; require transactional deduplication for external effects.

findings.title: Response exception mapping needs its own execution boundary
findings.evidence: Mappers run on an event loop by default; reading a blocking response stream needs the documented worker boundary.
findings.recommendation: Explain registration and Blocking mapper behavior instead of assuming async completion makes all processing safe.
findings.resolution: Explain registration and Blocking mapper behavior instead of assuming async completion makes all processing safe.

findings.title: Original knowledge checks had no answers
findings.evidence: Forty questions and eight proposed labs lacked worked answers and a runnable teaching baseline.
findings.recommendation: Answer all 40 and add a pinned original Java fixture with measured local execution and explicit larger-lab limits.
findings.resolution: Answer all 40 and add a pinned original Java fixture with measured local execution and explicit larger-lab limits.

blog_intake.value: Explains worker versus event-loop dispatch and why async signatures cannot justify blocking I/O.
blog_intake.limits: Historical article; use Jakarta imports and archived 3.8 behavior. Do not adopt old javax snippets or imply database-plus-Kafka transaction atomicity.

local_validation.java_execution_boundary: Actual local Quarkus HTTP/Panache/H2 tests; no remote platform or complete eight-lab execution.

local_validation.fixture_repair: Expanded private test fixture string escaping failed compilation and was fixed before successful tests.
